ratings_why.fun: Three builds with a clear seed-to-capstone arc each, and the Level gives every turn a real vote; happily drafted, though the swing build's late turns are a lot of trigger counting.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because the Flood is a visible, shared water level that takes a share of Health from both front rows, so you drown your own slots on purpose and enemy stats work against them; no tribe today or generic auto-battler plays like that.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken as written; the open questions are dials (tenths, cap, refloods) for the owner's balance pass, so more revising would mostly make it different.

points.text: The Spaarndam Pup with Tail-Slapper halves the whole enemy board three times a fight at Level 5; a good capstone ceiling, worth a Tier 6 sim before the owner sets the tenths.
Bench Coot puts you at Level 1 on turn 1, so the 'at least 1' floor pings every enemy front unit from the first fight; consider starting the floor at Level 2 if early fights feel decided by it.
Hendrika triggers on Raise or Drain, so Kobus Bles doubles her too; harmless (the second carry does nothing), but a line saying Kobus skips her would match the rationale.
With Hendrika, Kobus and Millwright, Old Bram gives about +60/+60 a turn to the smallest units; a fine high roll, but it drowns out the T5 job of the other two builds' payoffs.
The growth shape is good: steady +1/+1s early, a Tier 4 multiplier, then three different late payoffs (permanent stats, gold, enemy-Health shares).

standouts.why: Polder Millwright gives two changes without moving the Level, which makes the swing build and the raise/drain tension both work.
Aaltje Sluiswacht lets a drained board still Flood, a neat bridge between builds and a readable fight trick.
Drowned-Spire Coot turns the Flood into permanent growth and gives High Water its direction card.

weakest.why: Inspecting Heemraad is a plain per-turn buffer whose best case, Level 5, also floods the units it buffs.
Sluice Keeper's gold needs a Raise source each turn, so it often pays only every other turn.
Kees Kowk is in-fight Attack only and does less than Drowned-Spire Coot for the same build.

flags.note: Each extra Flood takes another share of enemy Health; with the Pup or a golden copy, the enemy board can be near-wiped before most attacks land.
Hendrika with Kobus and Nine Mills is about +14/+14 to every unit a turn; bounded, but the top of the tribe's ceiling.
Level 1 from turn 1 pops Shields and kills 1-Health units early, which may decide turns 2-4.
